"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"How do you treat recurrrent non healing ulcers in Diabetes?\u003Cdiv\u003ERecalcitrant non-healing ulcers are inevitable and detrimental to the lower limb and are a major cause of non-traumatic lower limb amputations. Application of autologous Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP) has been a major breakthrough for the treatment of non-healing and diabetic foot ulcers, as it is an easy and cost-effective method, and provides the necessary growth factors that enhance tissue healing. PRP is a conglomeration of thrombocytes, cytokines and various growth factors which are secreted by α-granules of platelets that augment the rate of natural healing process with decrease in time.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhat might be the cause of vomitings in a patient of Diabetes?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFactors related to your diabetes may cause you to experience nausea.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMedication:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMetformin is one of the more common medications used to treat diabetes. Nausea is a potential side effect for people taking this medication. Taking metformin on an empty stomach may make nausea worse.Injectable medications used to treat diabetes, such as exenatide (Byetta), liraglutide (Victoza), pramlintide (Symlin), and other glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonists may cause nausea.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EArtificial sweeteners and sugar alcohols:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn an attempt to manage blood sugars, many people with diabetes turn to artificial sweeteners and sugar alcohols to minimize their regular sugar intake.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHowever, a common side effect of added sweeteners, like xylitol is nausea, as well as other digestive symptoms. When someone has more than one serving per day,the side effects may be amplified.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAspartame, a popular artificial sweetener, can cause nausea.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETypes of MODY (Maturity onset diabetes of young)??\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; MUTATIONS\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;and\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;PHENOTYPES HNF4alpha - adolescent or early adult in onset: progressive in insulin secretory defect.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGLUCOKINASE-Since birth:stable mild fasting hyperglycemia\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHNF1alpha-adolescent or early adult in onset: progressive in insulin secretory defect.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIPF-1 - Early adult : mild Diabetes\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHNF-1beta- Adolescent: progressive diabetes\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENeuro D1- Early adult : rare\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EKLF11- Early adult : Pancreatic atrophy\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECEL,PAX4,INS,BLK.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELEARNING POINTS:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI learnt the pathophysiology of Type 1 and Type 2 DM\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI got to know how to diagnose between type 1 and Type 2 based on the treatment response shown by the patient\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI also learnt about the phenotypic features of different mutations in MODY\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI learnt about the various complications of Diabetes\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis case helped me to know the cause of recurrent healing ulcer, its association with diabetes and its management\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis case also helped me to know that it's important to evaluate side-effects of the drugs (overdosage) given and wrong medications taken by the patient which was prescribed by any RMPs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/145dilliswar.blogspot.com\/feeds\/2028138636553145112\/comments\/default","title":"Post signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIhave been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 40 years male, resident of chityala, field assistant by occupation came to the opd with chief complaints of vomitings 2 days back\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of presenting illness:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 2 days back and then he started developing vomitings ( 18 episodes till yesterday )\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENon bilious, non projectile, non blood stained in nature with watery consistency and is associated with squeezing feeling in the epigastrium region each time preceeding the vomiting episode.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo history of associated symptoms like fever, diarrhoea, chest pain, abdominal pain, abdominal distension, constipation, headache, giddiness.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPast history:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of diabetic ulcer on the heel since 2 months( healing) and on great toe since 1 month.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of diabetes mellitus since 6 months( on medication)and hypertension since 2 months( not on medication).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo history of asthma,CAD,Tuberculosis and epilepsy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETreatment history:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was on metformin 500mg since 6 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFamily history:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of diabetes mellitus in mother since 15 years and elder brother since 10 years.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPersonal history:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiet: mixed\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAppetite: normal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESleep: Adequate but interrupted during nights when he gets up to micturate\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBowel movements: normal\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBladder movements: Interrupted urine flow\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAddictions: Alcohol 180ml per day for 10 years and then stopped since 2 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EGeneral examination:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient is conscious coherent and cooperative\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EModerately built and Moderately nourished\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EVitals:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPulse: 72 bpm\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERR: 16cpm\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBp: 120\/80 mm Hg\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETemp: Afebrile\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo pallor, icterus,cyanosis,koilonychia, clubbing, generalised lymphadenopathy, pedal edema\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESystemic examination:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECVS : S1 S2 heard.
